messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Talk to your doctor if the pain you have increases.
Talk to your doctor if you feel more sensitive to pain.
Talk to your doctor if you have new pain after taking tramadol.
Tramadol extended-release capsules and tablets may complicate a healthcare provider’s clinical assessment of an acute abdominal condition.
They are not recommended for people with severe liver or severe kidney impairment.
Taking tramadol during pregnancy may cause life-threatening withdrawal symptoms in the newborn.
These symptoms are known as neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome (NOWS).
Some people are "ultra-rapid metabolizers" of tramadol.
This is because of a variation in an enzyme.
The enzyme is called CYP2D6.
People's bodies convert tramadol into tramadol's active form faster than usual.
This can produce dangerously high opioid levels.
This can occur even at a normal dose.
Life-threatening breathing problems and deaths have occurred in children for this reason.
This has happened including after surgery to remove the tonsils or adenoids.
Tramadol should not be given to a child younger than 12 years old.
Triples: [["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "talk to your doctor if pain increases"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "talk to your doctor if more sensitive to pain"], ["tramadol", "has administration instruction", "talk to your doctor if new pain occurs after taking"], ["tramadol extended-release capsules", "complicates", "clinical assessment of acute abdominal condition"], ["tramadol", "not recommended for", "people with severe liver impairment"], ["tramadol", "not recommended for", "people with severe kidney impairment"], ["tramadol", "has pregnancy or breastfeeding warning", "may cause life-threatening withdrawal symptoms in newborn"], ["tramadol", "has side effect", "neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome"], ["tramadol", "has variant metabolizer type", "ultra-rapid metabolizers"], ["tramadol", "has cause", "variation in an enzyme"], ["enzyme", "has name", "CYP2D6"], ["tramadol", "metabolized by", "CYP2D6"], ["tramadol", "converted into", "tramadol's active form"], ["tramadol", "has side effect", "dangerously high opioid levels"], ["tramadol", "has side effect", "life-threatening breathing problems"], ["tramadol", "has side effect", "deaths in children"], ["tramadol", "has side effect", "occurring after surgery to remove tonsils or adenoids"], ["tramadol", "not recommended for", "children younger than 12 years old"]]
Relations: ["complicates", "converted into", "has administration instruction", "has cause", "has name", "has pregnancy or breastfeeding warning", "has side effect", "has variant metabolizer type", "metabolized by", "not recommended for"]
Answer:

completion:
complicates: The subject entity may interfere with or make more difficult the clinical assessment or diagnosis of the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
converted into: The subject entity is transformed or chemically altered into the active or functional form specified by the object entity.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug has a specific instruction or guidance for its administration, as specified by the object entity.  
has cause: The subject entity is caused by or is a result of the factor or condition specified by the object entity.  
has name: The subject entity is identified or referred to by the name specified by the object entity.  
has pregnancy or breastfeeding warning: The subject drug has a specific warning or caution related to its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, as specified by the object entity.  
has side effect: The subject drug may cause the adverse or unintended effect specified by the object entity.  
has variant metabolizer type: The subject drug is associated with a specific type of metabolic variation in individuals, as specified by the object entity.  
metabolized by: The subject drug is processed or broken down by the enzyme or metabolic system specified by the object entity.  
not recommended for: The subject drug is not advised for use in individuals who have the condition or are in the group specified by the object entity.
